evidence: Walk the full track. Most walkers take 4 days/3 nights.
The track begins with a stroll through the beech forest along the shore of Lake Te Anau, the largest body of fresh water in Australasia, to Brod Bay.
The track then follows the Waiau River terrace to the swing bridge at Rainbow Reach.
Continue alongside the Waiau River to the Kepler Track car park.

doubts: Start and end: the Kepler Track car park has no road-end feature or named place entry (the Rainbow Reach road end F1 is used only for the Rainbow Reach car park), so the start and end refs are null; the walk is a loop, so the end is the same place. Direction: the text does not say clockwise or anticlockwise. The four day walks are separate DOC walk pages covering parts of the track and are listed as other walks, not ways. The Brod Bay Campsite (named in the Fees section as a campsite on the track) is on the way to Brod Bay but the text does not say the walk stays there, so it is not listed as a hut or via. The Luxmore Cave side trip is 'signposted' from the hut but has no feature or name match for certain, so its ref is null and its start is the hut as stated. The Luxmore summit side trip does not say which point it leaves from, so from is null; ref T13 is taken as Mount Luxmore. Forest Burn and Hanging Valley shelters are mentioned only as places where camping and staying are not permitted, and Rocky Point Shelter has no bunks mentioned, so neither is listed as a hut. Lake Manapouri and Lake Te Anau are named in the text with no name entry, so their refs are null. The 'Rainbow Reach car park' access point is matched to road end F1 by the nearest feature.
